record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: Around the QCD phase transition, what is the full temperature-dependent shape of the axion potential away from its minimum, especially near θ̄ = π where the low-temperature potential is cuspy, and how does that shape affect post-inflationary axion dynamics such as minicluster formation?

evidence.quote: Another area that requires more detailed analysis is how the axion potential turns on around the QCD phase transition [218]. There have been lattice computations that give the axion mass around the minimum as a function of temperature. However, there is no understanding of how the axion potential behaves away from 0 as a function of temperature.

The behavior of the axion potential near θ = π is important because if the axion field value started off near θ = π, then interesting dynamics such as axion miniclusters occur and may be interesting observationally. Because the axion expectation value is equally distributed, the behavior at large θ is necessarily important and should be explored.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider QCD with $N_f$ light quark flavors coupled to an axion field $a$ via the topological charge density, so that the QCD vacuum energy depends on the effective angle $\bar\theta = a/f_a$, where $f_a$ is the axion decay constant. Define the finite-temperature axion effective potential $V(\bar\theta,T)$ as the free energy density of QCD as a function of $\bar\theta$ at temperature $T$, normalized so that $V(0,T)=0$. At zero temperature, chiral perturbation theory predicts a $2\pi$-periodic potential that is smooth near $\bar\theta=0$ but develops a cusp at $\bar\theta=\pi$ (e.g.\ $V(\bar\theta,0) = -m_\pi^2 f_\pi^2\sqrt{1 - \frac{4 m_u m_d}{(m_u+m_d)^2}\sin^2(\bar\theta/2)}$ in the two-flavor case). At high temperatures, dilute-instanton calculations predict $V(\bar\theta,T) \approx \chi(T)(1-\cos\bar\theta)$ for some topological susceptibility $\chi(T)$.

Determine the full shape of $V(\bar\theta,T)$ for all $\bar\theta\in[0,2\pi)$ as a function of $T$ across the QCD crossover region (roughly $T\sim 100$–$300$ MeV), in particular:

(a) Describe quantitatively how the cusp at $\bar\theta=\pi$ present at $T=0$ smooths out (or persists) as $T$ increases through the QCD transition, and identify the temperature dependence of the second derivative $\partial^2 V/\partial\bar\theta^2$ and of the height $V(\pi,T)$.

(b) Using this potential, analyze the cosmological evolution of a post-inflationary axion field whose initial misalignment angle is near $\bar\theta=\pi$, and determine the consequences for the formation, abundance, and mass spectrum of axion miniclusters arising from the resulting nonlinear axion dynamics.
artifact.status_search_result: Lattice studies have determined the topological susceptibility (and hence the axion mass at the minimum) as a function of temperature through and above the QCD crossover, and recent work has begun to explore the $\bar\theta$ dependence in hot/dense media, finding flattening of the peak at $\bar\theta=\pi$. However, the full temperature-dependent shape of $V(\bar\theta,T)$ away from the minimum—especially the smoothing of the $T=0$ cusp at $\bar\theta=\pi$ across the QCD transition—and its detailed consequences for post-inflationary axion minicluster dynamics remain not fully established, so the question is best classified as open.

status_evidence.title: Calculation of the axion mass based on high-temperature lattice QCD
status_evidence.snippet: Lattice computation of topological susceptibility and axion mass as a function of temperature.
status_evidence.claim: Lattice gives axion mass (curvature of potential at minimum) versus T, but not full-shape information at general $\bar\theta$.

status_evidence.title: QCD topology and axion properties in an isotropic hot and dense medium
status_evidence.snippet: As chemical potential increases, both the height and sharpness of the peak at theta=pi are reduced, resulting in a broader and flatter profile.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work indicates the cusp/peak at $\bar\theta=\pi$ flattens with thermodynamic parameters, but a complete temperature-dependent shape across the QCD transition is still being investigated.

status_evidence.title: The topological susceptibility in finite temperature QCD and axion cosmology
status_evidence.snippet: Finite-T dependence of axion potential and mass computed up to crossover; instanton approach unreliable at higher T.
status_evidence.claim: Standard treatments compute susceptibility but emphasize unreliability of full-potential extrapolations, supporting that the shape away from the minimum is not yet fully understood.
